info.description: Runs security, performance, SEO, privacy and accessibility checks against a website. Each check returns a verdict: pass, warning, fail, or no verdict when it could not run. GET /checks lists them; POST /monitor/single runs a selection against one site, and GET /check/{name} runs a single check.
info.title: Website Monitor API

Redirect to the web interface under /docs/.

The page loads its stylesheet, script and fonts by relative path, and
those only exist under the /docs mount: served at /, every one of them

## Accessibility Check

Check the website's accessibility score using Lighthouse or similar services.

Order of attempts:
1. Lighthouse via the PageSpeed Insights API (key: api_key or PAGESPEED_API_KEY).
2. WAVE API, only when WAVE_API_KEY is set.
3. Local heuristics on the page HTML (result marked "(heuristic)").
Any API failure (HTTP error, 429 quota, malformed JSON) falls through to
the next step instead of raising.

Args:
- website (str): URL of the website to be checked.
- api_key (str, optional): PageSpeed Insights API key.

Returns:
- str: "🟢" if the accessibility score is high (0.9 to 1),
       "🟠" if the score is moderate (0.8 to 0.9),
       "🔴" if the score is low (less than 0.8),
       "⚪" for any errors.

**Category:** Accessibility

## Dns Blacklist Check

Check if a domain is blacklisted in known DNS-based blacklists.

Args:
    domain (str): The domain name to be checked.

Returns:
    str: 
        - "🟢" if the domain is not in any blacklist.
        - "🟡" if the domain is found in some blacklists.
        - "🔴" if the domain is found in multiple or critical blacklists.
        - "⚪" if no blacklist could give a verdict (or the IP is not public).
        A "(no verdict from ...)" suffix names lists that answered with an
        error code (e.g. Spamhaus 127.255.255.254 when queried through a
        public resolver); those lists are not counted as listings.

Note: these are IP-based DNSBLs. The domain's IPv4 address is queried,
so for a site behind a CDN the result describes the CDN edge IP.

**Category:** Domain

get.description:
## Mobile Friendly Check

Check if the given website is mobile-friendly from its HTML.

This used to call Google's Mobile-Friendly Test API, which needs a Search
Console API key the monitor never passes and whose retirement Google
announced for December 2023. It is now a local static check of the page
HTML. It does not render the page: it only reads markup and inline CSS.

Criteria:
    1. A <meta name="viewport"> exists and its content has
       width=device-width. Without it mobile browsers render the page at a
       desktop width (about 980px) and shrink it: 🔴.
    2. The viewport does not disable zooming (user-scalable=no or
       maximum-scale below 2): otherwise 🟡.
    3. No fixed-width layout hints: no "width: Npx" declaration with
       N >= 980 in <style> blocks or style attributes (max-width and
       min-width are ignored), and no width="N" attribute with N >= 980:
       otherwise 🟡.

Args:
    website (str): The URL or bare domain of the website to be checked.
    api_key (str, optional): Ignored, kept for backward compatibility.

Returns:
    str:
        - "🟢" if all criteria pass.
        - "🟡 (reasons)" if the viewport is responsive but there are issues.
        - "🔴 (no responsive viewport meta)" if criterion 1 fails.
        - "⚪" for any errors.

**Category:** Accessibility

parameters.name: website

schema.description: Website URL or domain to check with mobile_friendly

## Health Check

Get the current health status of the API, including:
- Service status
- Available checks count
- Configuration status
- Current server time

post.description:
## Comprehensive Website Monitoring

Run all available security, performance, and compliance checks on multiple websites.

**Features:**
- 50+ specialized checks per website
- Parallel execution for optimal performance
- Detailed results with status indicators
- Custom timeout configuration
- PageSpeed Insights integration (with API key)

**Result Indicators:**
- 🟢 Check passed
- 🔴 Check failed  
- 🟡 Check warning/partial
- ⚪ Check error/timeout

## Asynchronous Website Monitoring

Start monitoring checks in the background and return immediately with a task ID.
Useful for large batch jobs or when you don't want to wait for completion.

**Workflow:**
1. Submit monitoring request
2. Receive task ID immediately
3. Use task ID to check status via `/monitor/async/{task_id}`
4. Retrieve results when complete
